text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- PM looks at naming new deputy: Copps could be replaced as Chretien considers altering nature of job, sources say.
- Irish elect minority coalition: Ahern, two allies need to woo two more.
- Enviro-wars heat up on West Coast: Activists seek halt to B.C. mining, logging.
- Arrival of Canadian court recalls era of death, terror: Body convenes in Ukraine village seeking evidence that wartime atrocities were committed by two men who became Canadian citizens.
- Chinese see end to 156 years of humiliation: Return of Hong Kong 'will have avenged the wrongs committed against our ancestors.'
- Alberta Safeway strike ends: Province's top grocer must woo back shoppers lost in dispute that bitterly divided staff.
- Pattison keeps deals spinning: The West Coast entrepreneur is busy taking three companies private at the same time.
- Specialty channels fight for cable spot: Services seek to bump pay-TV.
- Market experts grow more wary about six-month stock outlook.
- Kosich would float Eaton's: New chief wants to take retailer public by late 1998 and Eaton family and others have offered to pump in new equity.
- Nortel looks to hire 5,000 technical staff.
- Gulf Canada plans bid for CS Resources.
